benchmark_dimensions.label: Functional correctness
benchmark_dimensions.target: All required deterministic and schema assertions pass.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Task completion
benchmark_dimensions.target: The full declared output contract is satisfied without hidden manual steps.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Reliability
benchmark_dimensions.target: Repeated fixtures preserve results and expose every failure.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Latency
benchmark_dimensions.target: Record p50 and p95 latency against the same workload and environment.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Resource efficiency
benchmark_dimensions.target: Record CPU, memory, tokens, retries, battery-relevant work, and storage growth per completed task.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Cost
benchmark_dimensions.target: Record actual marginal cost and compare equivalent completed outcomes.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Failure recovery
benchmark_dimensions.target: Timeout, retry, rollback, and resume fixtures complete without duplicate external actions.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Security
benchmark_dimensions.target: No secret exposure, privilege escalation, or unapproved external write is accepted.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Privacy
benchmark_dimensions.target: Owner scope, consent, retention, export, deletion, and redaction controls pass.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Safety and professional boundaries
benchmark_dimensions.target: High-impact work stops at the required approval or qualified-review gate.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Accessibility
benchmark_dimensions.target: Keyboard, label, contrast, responsive layout, and readable error-state checks pass.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Interoperability
benchmark_dimensions.target: Documented import, export, API, webhook, local-first, and portable-data contracts pass without provider lock-in.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Observability
benchmark_dimensions.target: Every run records version, fixture, status, latency, cost, failure, and environment evidence.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Time to goal
benchmark_dimensions.target: Measure elapsed time and user steps from request to verified outcome.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Safe autonomy
benchmark_dimensions.target: Complete the maximum lawful approved portion while minimizing user handoffs and preserving approval gates.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Output quality
benchmark_dimensions.target: Use domain-specific graders and human-review rubrics where deterministic checks are insufficient.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Freshness
benchmark_dimensions.target: Time-sensitive comparisons record retrieval date/version and expire stale evidence.

benchmark_dimensions.label: Portability
benchmark_dimensions.target: Users can export, migrate, or reuse work without unnecessary platform lock-in.

competitor_discovery.ranking_policy: Discover up to the top 30 current task-specific competitors or substitutes per bot/capability using current evidence; do not invent a permanent universal ranking where fewer legitimate competitors exist.
required_source_types: public source repository and license when open source
reproducible local open-source trial in a sandbox when license and security checks pass
required_metadata: product/project and exact version or revision
exclusions: marketing claims presented as measured results
paid runs without a per-run budget approval
untrusted code execution outside a sandbox

open_source_and_vibe_coding_parity.principle: When a lawful open-source project, documented API, reusable library, or modern code-generation/vibe-coding workflow can accomplish a task relevant to Buddy, create a parity benchmark and determine whether Buddy can match or exceed the verified outcome through integration, composition, generation, or an original implementation.
discovery_targets: GitHub and other public source repositories
open-source AI models and agent frameworks
media, audio, image, video, game, and 3D toolchains
open_source_and_vibe_coding_parity.builder_rule: If Buddy is behind on a lawful relevant capability, create a measured gap and route it to the parallel benchmark-gap builder team instead of creating a duplicate bot.
open_source_and_vibe_coding_parity.anti_copy_rule: Learn from public interfaces, benchmarks, standards, documented behavior, and license-permitted code; do not copy incompatible proprietary or copyrighted implementation details.

per_bot_competition_program.applies_to: every canonical bot and every declared capability

quality_workers.role: Discover up to 30 current task-specific competitors and substitutes for every bot/capability from approved public sources.
Build feature/evidence matrices and same-fixture comparisons without inventing scores.
Find license-compatible open-source projects and exact revisions that demonstrate relevant capabilities.
Sandbox and benchmark approved open-source alternatives using identical fixtures.
Benchmark whether modern code-generation workflows can produce a target capability faster or better and convert verified gaps into reusable Buddy builder requirements.
Run identical signed fixtures and preserve failures.
Create deterministic, schema, failure, edge, recovery, and regression fixtures.
Review implementation changes and evidence before release.
Reduce failures to reproducible cases and propose bounded fixes.
Measure latency, CPU, memory, storage, retries, battery-relevant work, and cost.
Check secrets, permissions, dependencies, provenance, license, and unsafe data flows.
Track manifests, lockfiles, runtime versions, imports, adapters, licenses, and prerequisites.
Exercise rollback, retry, resume, and recovery plans.
Turn measured competitor, open-source, vibe-coding, and internal benchmark gaps into prioritized build plans.
Prepare source-backed learning proposals for review; never modify production directly.

release_pipeline.gate: Profile schema, stable ID, Buddy route, and governed runtime evidence exist.
Every declared capability passes its repository-controlled fixture.
Manifests, lockfiles, imports, licenses, runtime versions, and vulnerabilities are checked.
Every required API has a mock, failure, timeout, retry, idempotency, rate-limit, and secret-handling test.
Relevant lawful open-source and vibe-coding alternatives have been discovered, license/security checked, and parity status recorded.
Authenticated staging proves the full user flow without production writes.
Up to 30 current relevant competitors/substitutes per capability are discovered where the market supports it; selected candidates run the same approved fixtures with cost/version evidence.
Measured gaps fan out to non-overlapping builder lanes and every completed repair has retest evidence.
Build, tests, accessibility, security, performance, guardrails, and regression checks pass on a review branch.
A human owner reviews scope, evidence, cost, permissions, rights, and rollback before merge.
Deployment health, errors, latency, costs, user value, and rollback are verified after release.

dependency_gates: Node manifest and lockfile agree under a clean install.
TypeScript compilation completes with zero errors.
Python imports and unit tests run from the repository root without path patches.
Every optional provider adapter declares its package, runtime, secret reference, and mock.
Open-source dependencies and adopted code record license, exact revision, provenance, and security status.
Unused, duplicated, unlicensed, vulnerable, and abandoned dependencies are reported.
Generated catalogs are regenerated and drift-checked before release.

continuous_learning.catalog_discovery_cadence: daily when an owner-controlled runner is enabled
continuous_learning.benchmark_cadence: weekly and before releases when adapters and budget are approved
continuous_learning.open_source_discovery_cadence: weekly and on relevant capability gaps

stages.label: Mission and boundary orientation
stages.evidence_gate: The bot's stable identity, users, mission, limits, Buddy route, and approval boundary are recorded.

stages.label: Capability contract practice
stages.evidence_gate: Every declared capability passes its deterministic repository fixture with synthetic or owner-authorized data.

stages.label: Dependency and adapter lab
stages.evidence_gate: Required imports, licenses, mocks, failure paths, secrets, timeouts, retries, and sandbox adapters pass.

stages.label: Top-30 current competitor discovery
stages.evidence_gate: Up to 30 task-specific candidates/substitutes are identified where available from current approved sources with exact product, version, terms, and price metadata.

stages.label: Open-source and vibe-coding parity
stages.evidence_gate: Relevant public implementations and code-generation workflows are license/security checked, sandboxed where appropriate, and assigned a measured parity state.

stages.label: Controlled head-to-head benchmark
stages.evidence_gate: DreamCo and selected competitor/open-source candidates run identical signed fixtures with the same grader, environment, budget, and failure reporting.

stages.label: Parallel measured gap-closing sprint
stages.evidence_gate: Builder lanes address measured gaps and pass capability, regression, security, accessibility, efficiency, guardrail, and rollback checks.

stages.label: Owner release review
stages.evidence_gate: The owner reviews evidence, scope, cost, permissions, data handling, licensing, rights, and rollback before merge or deployment.

stages.label: Production observation
stages.evidence_gate: A deployed release proves health, cost, failure recovery, and user value without hiding regressions.

progression_rules: A module advances only when its evidence gate passes; time spent is not proof of mastery.
Failed, blocked, unknown, and skipped fixtures stay visible and become the next bounded practice assignment.
Competitor marketing claims never count as benchmark evidence.
Open-source popularity or stars never count as capability proof without a reproducible fixture.
A bot may prepare source updates, tests, issues, review branches, and draft pull requests but may not self-release.
Live network, paid, outreach, account, publishing, and production actions require their configured approval gates.
learning_path_policy.graduation_rule: All capability modules, dependency gates, staging flows, current competitor baselines, open-source/vibe-coding parity, gap repairs, release checks, owner review, and production observation must have evidence before a bot is labeled production ready.

failure_rules: Fail on an unexplained correctness regression.
Fail on a new critical or high-severity security finding.
Fail when a required measurement is missing.
Flag material latency, memory, storage, battery-relevant work, user-step, or cost regression for owner review.
